sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 4.7 and its proof, p.14 (with Definition 3.2, p.9), in the author final version (33 pp., revised 9 December 2021, SHA-256 d95100eb…546f; identical to arXiv 1904.06512v2)
sourceIssues.printed: "Lemma 4.7. If 2 ≤ n ≤ 6, the outer exponent of U¹ is equal to p. Proof. As the abelianization of U¹ has exponent p when n ≥ 2, the outer exponent of U¹ is divisible by p."
sourceIssues.correction: For 2 ≤ n ≤ 6 the powering action of (Z/d)^× on conjugacy classes of U¹ factors through (Z/p)^×; hence the outer exponent is p for p odd and 1 for p = 2.
sourceIssues.reason: Definition 3.2 takes the least divisor e of the exponent through which the action factors. For p = 2, (Z/2)^× = (Z/1)^× is trivial and the proof shows the action is trivial (n ≤ 3 by Lemma 4.6; 4 ≤ n ≤ 6 because M^{−1} is conjugate to M), so e = 1, not 2; the divisibility step holds only for odd p. The lemma is used only to make the cyclotomic character χ : G → (Z/e)^× trivial when μ_p ⊂ k and to choose L ⊇ μ_e, which is unchanged for e = 1 since μ₂ ⊂ k; the main theorems are unaffected. Noted by the extraction (items 42, 65).

sourceIssues.locator: Proofs of Theorem 5.1 (p.22) and Theorem 7.4 (p.28), with the definition of local field on p.19, in the author final version (33 pp., revised 9 December 2021, SHA-256 d95100eb…546f; identical to arXiv 1904.06512v2)
sourceIssues.printed: "We are thus reduced to checking that W(k_v) ≠ ∅ for any place v of k … which is exactly what Proposition 5.3 provides when applied to the restriction of α to each Γ_{k_v}", while p.19 says: "Here and below, by a local field, we mean a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field."
sourceIssues.correction: Treat the archimedean places separately. For v complex, Γ_{k_v} is trivial. For v real and p odd, U/P^{r,s} is a p-group, so the restriction of α to Γ_{k_v} ≅ C₂ is trivial. For v real and p = 2, the proof of Proposition 5.3 goes through: the split case is group theory, and in the non-split case H¹(R, Hom(P/Z, μ₂)) × H¹(R, P/Z) → H²(R, μ₂) is perfect (Tate duality over R), so cup product with [γ] is onto.
sourceIssues.reason: The global argument needs local solvability at every place, but Proposition 5.3 is stated only for non-archimedean fields; the real places with p = 2 need an argument, which is short. Noted by the extraction (items 91, 117).

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 5.5, p.19, in the author final version (33 pp., revised 9 December 2021, SHA-256 d95100eb…546f; identical to arXiv 1904.06512v2)
sourceIssues.printed: "Let Γ be a profinite group and 0 → A → B → C → 0 be a short exact sequence of discrete Γ-modules whose underlying sequence of abelian groups is split. … Let [γ] ∈ H¹(Γ, Hom(C,A)) be the class of this torsor"
sourceIssues.correction: Assume C finitely generated (for example finite, as in the only application, C = P^{r,s}/Z). Otherwise Hom(C,A) with the discrete topology need not carry a continuous class.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: Γ = ∏ C₂ (countably many factors), A = ⊕ F₂a_i and C = ⊕ F₂c_i with trivial action, B = A ⊕ C with g·c_i = c_i + g_i a_i. B is a discrete module and the sequence splits as groups, but γ(g)(c_i) = g_i a_i has kernel {1}, which is not open, so γ is not continuous into the discrete module Hom(C,A). Found by the extraction (item 139).
